newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - July 9.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - July 9.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Philippine stocks on Wednesday:
* Philippine shares are likely to remain wobbly as high domestic interest rates and nervousness in the foreign exchange market will keep investors out of the market, brokers said.
* A Sun Hung Kai Securities report said market players were still wary over the high interest rates.
"Two more days of declines could bring us toward the established 2,650 support," it said.
* Magnum International Securities analyst Julie Villena, however, said she could not discount the possibility of a slight technical rally.
The composite index slipped through its 2,700 psychological support on Tuesday to close at 2,698.66.
She said the strong Wall Street rally last night could trigger some buying, especially in dollar-sensitive companies such as Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co and export firms.
* On Monday, the Dow Jones rose 103.81 points to 7,962.31.
* The peso closed 26.40 to the dollar vs Tuesday's close of 26.397.
* The Philippine Stock Exchange composite index fell 54.49 points to 2,698.66.
* The Philippine overnight money rose to 30.0625 percent from 24.53125 percent.
* Cash-strapped Victorias Milling Co is expecting a big loss this year but hopes to recover next year under its proposed financial rehabilitation programme, Manila Times says.
* Pilipino Telephone Corp announces the election of Roberto Ongpin as the chairman of its Board of directors.
* The two-year note coupon rose to 13.75 percent from the previous 11.625 percent, the Bureau of Treasury says.
* Manila Electric Co can post higher net income for the first half of 1997 despite slower sales growth, a Reuters poll says.
* Philippine National Bank employees stage a strike over pay package.
